# From the Rankin \(\kappa\)-kernel to the xi Pick kernel

**Fifth-stage investigation — 14 October 2026**<br>
**Question:** Can the positive kernel generated by \(\kappa_{\rm R}=1/(4\pi^2)\) be transformed into the RH-equivalent xi Pick kernel?<br>
**Companion program:** `scripts/research-rss-kappa-pick-transform.mjs`<br>
**Machine-readable results:** `docs/rh/rss-kappa-pick-transform-results.json`

## Result

An exact route has been found:

\[
\boxed{
K_\kappa
\longrightarrow
\text{stationary-increment Green geometry}
\longrightarrow
G_g
\xrightarrow{\ \mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L\ }
K_\xi.}
\]

The final arrow is an exact double Laplace identity, not an analogy. It makes the arithmetic screw kernel
\[
G_g(x,y)=\Psi(x)+\Psi(y)-\Psi(x-y)
\]
map to
\[
K_\xi(s,t)=
\frac{\xi'(s)/\xi(s)+\overline{\xi'(t)/\xi(t)}}
{s+\overline t-1}.
\]

Unconditionally, the transform converges in \(\Re s,\Re t>1\). If \(G_g\) were proved positive semidefinite on every real window, the same transform would become a Gram representation throughout \(\Re s,\Re t>1/2\) and would prove RH.

That global positivity has not been proved. It is a known form of the Riemann problem, expressed here in the geometry naturally selected by the Rankin coupling. The successful part of this stage is therefore an **exact kernel conversion and a sharper proof target**, not a proof of RH.

**Sixth-stage follow-up:** [Attempting global positivity of the Riemann screw kernel](./rss-global-screw-positivity-attempt.md) derives the exact recovery-witness cost/capacity and arrival-centroid targets, reproduces the classical Chebyshev bridge, and proves two RSS-specific obstructions: delayed prime hinges are operator-indefinite and primitive extraction from the repetition ledger is signed.

**Source-forensic follow-up:** [Audit of the earlier positivity lemma](./rss-earlier-positivity-lemma-audit.md) identifies the exact valid universal Gram statement as the \(D_{\kappa,\sigma}\) lemma in section 1, audits the older complete-monotonicity and Bernstein claims, and confirms that none supplies global positivity of \(G_g\).

**Entropy follow-up:** [The kappa-entropy splice audit](./rss-kappa-entropy-splice.md) keeps this derived kernel fixed and tests the decimal identity/reflection channel. It obtains strict binary data processing and completed-\(\xi\)-ledger invariance, but the fixed-point set contains every reflection-symmetric off-line quartet and the feature barycentre is not the contracted feature.

---

## 1. The \(\kappa\)-kernel already has the right geometric type

The fourth-stage investigation obtained
\[
K_\kappa(s,t)
=\kappa_{\rm R}\zeta(s+\overline t+2),
\qquad
\kappa_{\rm R}=\frac1{4\pi^2},
\]
with feature vector
\[
v_s(n)=\sqrt{\kappa_{\rm R}}\,n^{-s-1}.
\]

Restrict to a vertical line, \(s=\sigma+i\tau\). Then
\[
v_{\sigma+i\tau}(n)
=\sqrt{\kappa_{\rm R}}\,n^{-\sigma-1}
 e^{-i\tau\log n}.
\]
Consequently, the increment kernel
\[
D_{\kappa,\sigma}(x,y)
=
\left\langle
v_{\sigma+ix}-v_\sigma,
 v_{\sigma+iy}-v_\sigma
\right\rangle
\]
is
\[
D_{\kappa,\sigma}(x,y)
=\kappa_{\rm R}
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n^{-2\sigma-2}
\left(e^{-ix\log n}-1\right)
\left(e^{iy\log n}-1\right).
\]

This is automatically positive semidefinite. It is the Gram kernel of a path with translation-invariant increments—a **screw line** in the terminology of Kreĭn and Suzuki.

Thus \(K_\kappa\) does not merely give an arbitrary positive matrix. It already supplies the correct geometric category:

- a positive Green weight;
- inverse-square smoothing;
- a unitary translation parameter;
- stationary increments; and
- a squared-distance kernel of negative type.

Its defect is spectral. Its frequencies are \(\log n\), with the smooth positive weights \(\kappa_{\rm R}n^{-2\sigma-2}\). The xi kernel requires the arithmetic spectrum produced by the complete explicit formula.

## 2. Why a simple bounded transform cannot work

Before constructing the successful transform, one can rule out a tempting shortcut.

For \(\Re s\ge1/2\),
\[
K_\kappa(s,s)
=\kappa_{\rm R}\zeta(2\Re s+2)
\le \kappa_{\rm R}\zeta(3).
\]
So the source feature vectors remain uniformly bounded as the critical boundary is approached.

By contrast, let
\[
\rho=\frac12+i\gamma
\]
be any known critical-line zero of multiplicity \(m\). For \(s=\rho+\varepsilon\),
\[
\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(s)
\sim\frac{m}{\varepsilon},
\]
and hence
\[
K_\xi(s,s)
\sim\frac{m}{\varepsilon^2}.
\]
The target feature norm is unbounded near every boundary zero.

Therefore there cannot be one bounded operator \(T\) satisfying
\[
K_\xi(s,t)=\langle T v_t,Tv_s\rangle
\]
on the full critical half-plane. A bounded operator could not send a uniformly bounded family to one with these boundary singularities.

This proves:

> **Bounded-transform no-go.** Converting \(K_\kappa\) into \(K_\xi\) requires an unbounded inverse-Green operation, a change of feature space, or both. Scalar rescaling, a bounded multiplier and ordinary kernel compression cannot suffice.

This explains why multiplying by the already-derived value of \(\kappa\), although geometrically important, could not by itself move the zeta argument or create the xi poles.

## 3. The arithmetic deformation: the Riemann screw potential

The needed replacement for the log-integer screw line is defined directly from prime powers and the archimedean completion.

For \(t\ge0\), put
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi(t)={}&4\left(e^{t/2}+e^{-t/2}-2\right)
-\sum_{n\le e^t}
\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}(t-\log n)\\
&+\frac t2
\left[
\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}\!\left(\frac14\right)-\log\pi
\right]\\
&+\frac14\left[
C-e^{-t/2}\Phi\!\left(e^{-2t},2,\frac14\right)
\right],
\end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
C=\pi^2+8G
\]
and \(G\) is Catalan’s constant. Extend \(\Psi\) evenly to the real line and define
\[
g(t)=-\Psi(t).
\]

This formula uses no zero locations. Its ingredients are:

- the von Mangoldt weights \(\Lambda(n)\), hence primitive prime powers;
- the gamma/digamma completion;
- the inverse-square Hurwitz–Lerch tail; and
- the same type of integrated Green response that \(\kappa_{\rm R}\) already selects.

The associated stationary-increment kernel is
\[
\boxed{
G_g(x,y)
=g(x-y)-g(x)-g(-y)+g(0)
=\Psi(x)+\Psi(y)-\Psi(x-y).}
\]

Masatoshi Suzuki proved that RH is equivalent to \(g\) being a screw function on all of \(\mathbb R\), meaning precisely
\[
G_g\succeq0
\]
for every finite real point set. For this particular arithmetic function he also obtained the striking scalar equivalent
\[
\boxed{
\mathrm{RH}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Psi(t)\ge0
\text{ for every real }t.}
\]
The scalar statement is not generally equivalent to kernel positivity for an arbitrary function; it is a special theorem for this \(\Psi\).

## 4. The exact one-sided transform

Let
\[
H(s)=\frac{\xi'(s)}{\xi(s)}
\]
and set \(s=1/2+w\). Suzuki’s Fourier–Laplace formula becomes
\[
\boxed{
H\!\left(\frac12+w\right)
=w^2\int_0^\infty\Psi(x)e^{-wx}\,dx.}
\]

Unconditionally this integral converges for \(\Re w>1/2\), corresponding to \(\Re s>1\). The identity follows from the explicit formula: the prime hinge
\[
(t-\log n)_+
\]
has Laplace transform
\[
\int_{\log n}^{\infty}(t-\log n)e^{-wt}\,dt
=\frac{n^{-w}}{w^2},
\]
so multiplication by \(w^2\) recovers
\[
-\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\Lambda(n)n^{-w-1/2}
=\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}\!\left(\frac12+w\right).
\]
The elementary, digamma and Hurwitz–Lerch terms recover the remaining factors in \(\xi'/\xi\).

This is the first exact answer to the user’s question: the missing logarithmic derivative is obtained by applying the inverse Green factor \(w^2\) to the Laplace transform of the arithmetic \(\kappa\)-type potential.

## 5. The double transform gives \(K_\xi\)

The one-variable formula upgrades to the desired two-variable kernel.

Let
\[
w=s-\frac12,
\qquad
v=\overline t-\frac12.
\]
For an even function \(g\), direct division of the first quadrant into \(x>y\) and \(y>x\) gives
\[
\int_0^\infty\!\int_0^\infty
 g(x-y)e^{-wx-vy}\,dx\,dy
=
\frac{\mathcal Lg(w)+\mathcal Lg(v)}{w+v}.
\]
Since \(g(0)=0\), it follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_0^\infty\!\int_0^\infty
G_g(x,y)e^{-wx-vy}\,dx\,dy\\
&\qquad=
\frac{H(\tfrac12+w)+H(\tfrac12+v)}
{wv(w+v)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Multiplication by \(wv\) yields
\[
\boxed{
K_\xi(s,t)
=(s-\tfrac12)(\overline t-\tfrac12)
\int_0^\infty\!\int_0^\infty
G_g(x,y)
 e^{-(s-1/2)x-(\overline t-1/2)y}
\,dx\,dy.}
\]

This is the requested exact conversion.

If \(G_g\) is a Gram kernel, the double Laplace map is a congruence: for any finite coefficients \(c_j\), its quadratic form is the norm of the corresponding Laplace-weighted combination of screw-line increments. It therefore preserves positivity and gives
\[
K_\xi\succeq0.
\]
That would exclude every zero in \(\Re s>1/2\).

## 6. Where the Rankin value \(\kappa_{\rm R}\) enters exactly

Assuming RH only for the purpose of displaying the conditional spectral decomposition, write the zero frequencies as
\[
q_\gamma=\frac{\gamma}{2\pi}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac1{\gamma^2}
=\frac{1}{4\pi^2}\frac1{q_\gamma^2}
=\frac{\kappa_{\rm R}}{q_\gamma^2}.
\]
The screw potential becomes
\[
\boxed{
\Psi(t)
=\kappa_{\rm R}
\sum_\gamma
\frac{1-\cos(2\pi q_\gamma t)}{q_\gamma^2}.}
\]
Similarly,
\[
G_g(x,y)
=\kappa_{\rm R}
\sum_\gamma
\frac{
(e^{2\pi i q_\gamma x}-1)
(e^{-2\pi i q_\gamma y}-1)}
{q_\gamma^2}.
\]

Thus the feature map is
\[
F_x(q_\gamma)
=
\sqrt{\kappa_{\rm R}}
\frac{e^{2\pi i q_\gamma x}-1}{q_\gamma}.
\]

This is exactly the unit-period Green feature selected by the framework’s value
\[
\kappa_{\rm R}=(2\pi)^{-2}.
\]
The integer cusp frequencies have been deformed into the normalised Riemann frequencies \(q_\gamma\). The value of \(\kappa\) is therefore not incidental: it is the universal inverse-square normalisation in the desired xi feature map.

The circularity is also now completely visible. Writing this sum as a positive Gram expansion assumes that every \(q_\gamma\) is real. The arithmetic formula for \(\Psi\) avoids assuming that, but its global positivity remains to be proved.

## 7. Why the identity is not yet a proof

There are two different statements:

1. **Kernel equality:** the double Laplace transform equals \(K_\xi\).
2. **Kernel positivity:** \(G_g\) is positive semidefinite on every real window.

The first has now been established exactly. The second is equivalent to RH.

Unconditionally, \(\Psi(t)\) is known to obey a bound of the form
\[
\Psi(t)
\ll e^{t/2-c\sqrt t},
\]
so the ordinary Laplace integrals above converge only for \(\Re w>1/2\). Under RH, \(\Psi\) is bounded, and they converge for every \(\Re w>0\), which is exactly the desired half-plane.

One cannot simply analytically continue the integral and retain positivity. Analytic continuation preserves identities of holomorphic functions; it does not preserve Gram representations or signs of quadratic forms.

Likewise, the inverse-Green operation needed to remove the \(n^{-2}\) smoothing is unbounded. This is consistent with the boundary-growth no-go in Section 2.

## 8. The sharp remaining RSS theorem

The new minimal theorem is more concrete than the previous abstract request for vectors \(V_s\).

> **RSS arithmetic screw-line theorem.** Construct from primitive return and seam data a Hilbert space \(\mathcal H_{\rm RSS}\) and a path \(X:\mathbb R\to\mathcal H_{\rm RSS}\) such that
> \[
> \langle X(x)-X(0),X(y)-X(0)\rangle
> =\Psi(x)+\Psi(y)-\Psi(x-y)
> \]
> for every real \(x,y\), where \(\Psi\) is defined by the prime-power and archimedean formula above.

If this identity were independently derived, then \(G_g\) would be a Gram kernel by construction. The double Laplace identity would immediately produce the required feature map for \(K_\xi\).

In operator terms, write
\[
\Psi=\Psi_{\rm arch}-\Psi_{\rm prime}.
\]
The proof burden is a global domination theorem
\[
G_{\rm arch}^{(a)}
\succeq
G_{\rm prime}^{(a)}
\qquad\text{on every window }[-a,a].
\]
A Schur-complement or contractive-coupling proof of this inequality would be sufficient. Positivity on one fixed window, or for finitely many test vectors, is not.

## 9. Reducing pointwise positivity to prime-power checkpoints

The scalar target \(\Psi(t)\ge0\) can be sharpened further. Write
\[
\Psi(t)=A(t)-
\sum_{n\le e^t}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}(t-\log n),
\]
where \(A\) contains the elementary and archimedean terms. Between consecutive prime-power events the second term is linear, so
\[
\Psi''(t)=A''(t).
\]
Putting \(x=e^t\), direct differentiation of the Hurwitz–Lerch series gives
\[
\boxed{
A''(\log x)
=\frac{x^3-x-1}{\sqrt{x}(x^2-1)}.}
\]
The numerator changes sign at the plastic constant
\[
\varrho^3=\varrho+1,
\qquad
\varrho=1.324717\ldots<2.
\]
Therefore every interval after the first prime-power event \(x=2\) is strictly convex.

Suzuki’s Theorem 4.1 proves positivity on an initial interval extending beyond \(\log2\), so the pre-event segment is already controlled unconditionally.

At an event \(q=p^k\), \(\Psi\) stays continuous while its derivative falls by
\[
\frac{\Lambda(q)}{\sqrt q}.
\]
On each interval between consecutive prime powers there is consequently at most one interior minimum. The continuum problem reduces to one constrained checkpoint per interval:

- the left endpoint if the derivative is already nonnegative;
- the right endpoint if it remains nonpositive; or
- the unique zero of \(A'(t)-\sum_{n\le q}\Lambda(n)/\sqrt n\).

The verifier exhausts all \(15{,}040\) such intervals through \(t=12\), corresponding to prime powers through \(162{,}755\). Every computed constrained minimum is positive; the smallest is approximately
\[
0.02752
\]
at \(t\approx8.03906\), or \(e^t\approx3099.71\), between the events 3089 and 3109.

This is stronger than grid sampling because each complete inter-event interval is reduced by convexity to its actual candidate minimum. It remains a finite floating-point computation, not an infinite-tail proof or a directed-rounding certificate.

## 10. Reproducible diagnostics

The companion program evaluates \(\Psi\) from its arithmetic formula without using zeta zeros. It:

- sieves prime powers through \(162{,}755\), sufficient for \(0\le t\le12\);
- checks 600 positive sampled values of \(\Psi(t)\);
- uses exact inter-event convexity to locate and check the constrained minima of 15,040 complete prime-power intervals;
- checks four finite screw matrices, all with positive LDL pivots;
- independently evaluates \(\xi'/\xi\) on the real axis;
- numerically verifies
  \[
  H(1/2+w)=w^2\mathcal L\Psi(w)
  \]
  at three values, with maximum discrepancy below \(10^{-5}\);
- verifies three double-Laplace values of \(K_\xi\), with maximum discrepancy below \(3\times10^{-6}\); and
- records the bounded-transform obstruction.

These finite checks validate the formulas and implementation. They do not prove \(\Psi(t)\ge0\) for unbounded \(t\), nor positivity of every finite screw matrix.

## 11. Final answer

There **is** a way to make the \(\kappa\)-based Green geometry produce the xi Pick kernel:

1. turn the vertical restriction of \(K_\kappa\) into its stationary-increment kernel;
2. apply the Riemann explicit-formula deformation, replacing the smoothed log-integer spectrum by the arithmetic screw potential \(\Psi\);
3. centre it to form \(G_g(x,y)=\Psi(x)+\Psi(y)-\Psi(x-y)\); and
4. apply the double Laplace congruence.

The resulting expression is exactly \(K_\xi\). The Rankin value \(1/(4\pi^2)\) is exactly the inverse-square frequency normalisation in the conditional xi feature map.

The unsolved step is no longer equality of kernels. It is proving that the explicitly known arithmetic function \(\Psi\) is a squared Hilbert-space displacement—or, equivalently for this function, that
\[
\Psi(t)\ge0
\quad\text{for every real }t.
\]
That statement excludes every off-critical zero and is equivalent to RH.
